title: Inbox-to-Quote for Freight Forwarders
summary: Forwarders retype dozens of quote-request emails a day. AI reads them, prices them from the rate table and drafts the reply in a minute.
hook: "Need a price: 2 pallets, Bucharest → Hamburg, pickup Thursday." Whoever answers first gets the load.
story:
**Tom runs a 10-person freight forwarding company.** Every day his inbox gets **60–100 emails** asking for prices: different formats, attachments, in English, German, Polish and more. A dispatcher reads each one, copies the route, weight and dates into a spreadsheet, checks rates, calculates and writes a reply.

Each quote takes **10–20 minutes**. By the time they answer, a faster competitor has often already won the load. Good dispatchers are expensive, and they spend half their day **retyping emails**.

whyReal.title: Volume is huge
whyReal.text: Forwarders and brokers handle a constant stream of quote requests by email every day.

whyReal.title: First answer wins
whyReal.text: In spot freight, the quickest reasonable quote often gets the job, so speed is revenue.

whyReal.title: Messy input, perfect for AI
whyReal.text: Emails are unstructured and multilingual. LLMs are now good enough to extract route, weight, dates and cargo type reliably.

whyReal.title: Lots of small players
whyReal.text: Thousands of small forwarders across Europe and beyond still run on email, Excel and phone.

whoPays.label: Customer
whoPays.text: freight forwarders and transport brokers with 3–50 staff.

whoPays.label: Start market
whoPays.text: EU and UK forwarders, sold in English by Jonatan. Victor can help with Romanian/Russian-speaking companies as a bonus market.

solution.title: Connect inbox
solution.text: the company connects its Gmail or Outlook quote inbox.

solution.title: Read
solution.text: AI reads every request email and attachment and extracts origin, destination, weight, pallets, dates and cargo type.

solution.title: Price
solution.text: it calculates a price from the company's own rate table (per km, per pallet, per zone) plus margin rules.

solution.title: Draft
solution.text: a reply in the customer's language is ready in seconds.

solution.title: Approve
solution.text: the dispatcher checks it and clicks Send. Unclear requests are flagged with a question for the customer.

solution.title: Track
solution.text: a dashboard shows quotes sent, answered and won, and the win rate.

timeline.what: **Validate.** Jonatan calls 15+ forwarders (in English), Victor joins some calls on the tech side. We collect 50 real anonymised quote emails. We test the AI extraction on them by hand.
Inbox connection, extraction, rate table, draft replies.
Approve screen, dashboard, first 3 pilot companies.

risks.answer: Start with simple rate tables; the human always approves.
Concierge pilot: we process their emails for 2 weeks and show the time saved.
Read-only access to one inbox, EU hosting, data processing agreement.
He leads the calls in English; Victor joins to answer technical questions. Logistics groups on LinkedIn are a good start.

questions: How many quote requests do you get per day, and through which channels?
How long does one quote take? Who does it?
How many quotes do you lose because you answered too late?
How do you calculate prices today: Excel, gut feeling, software?
Would you let a tool read your quote inbox if it saved 3 hours a day?
